title: Two Russian Kh-101 missiles and a jet drone crash in Poland; Denmark expels Russian attaché over murder plot; rung holds at 4
bottom_line: Spillover risk is unchanged at rung 4 (deadly or deliberate incident), resting on October's deadly drone strike on a ship off Romania. Two Russian Kh-101 cruise missiles and a jet-powered drone crashed in south-eastern Poland during a Russian attack on Ukraine of more than 400 drones and 110 missiles. No one was hurt. Tusk said it looks like an intentional provocation; Trump called it a mistake. Denmark expelled Russia's defence attaché over a foiled plot to kill a Ukrainian-American rapper. The 30-day chance of a step up to rung 5 stays remote (5%).

ladder.rationale: Rung 4 rests on the deadly Khoryv strike off Constanța (INC-2026-0109, 23 October), still inside the 30-day window. The Polish crashes would be rung 3. Rung 5 needs deliberate, sustained Russian action against an ally, and no Polish official has said Poland was the target.

pathways.rationale: Base: 4 logged in 30 days against a 14-a-month baseline, with no serious case in 12 months. We raise it 5 points because two Kh-101s crashed in Poland, one several hundred metres from buildings, and Tusk called it intentional.

Base: 2 in 30 days against 1.7 a month, with 1 serious case in 12 months. We raise it 5 points because Denmark's PET says Russian intelligence planned a killing in Denmark, the week after Poland's foiled mass-casualty plot.
Base: 12 serious cases in 12 months, and 15 ships hit off Bulgaria and Romania since October. We found no new hit in the window. Radev says Bulgaria cannot detect or destroy the drones. Held.
Base: no incidents in 30 days against 0.7 a month, and no serious case in 12 months. Nothing new in the window. Held.
Base: zero baseline, and no crossing of a NATO border since 2022. Estonian intelligence says Russian recruitment cannot keep up with front-line losses. Held.
Base: 1 plant-safety event in 30 days against 0.3 a month, and no serious case. We could not open IAEA Update 376, and found no new loss of power. Held.
Base: no incidents in 30 days against 0.3 a month. Nothing new blocks a NATO or EU decision. Held.

countries.reason: At floor. Two Kh-101s and a jet drone crashed on Polish soil, a rung-3 case not yet logged. That is consistent with Elevated.
One above the floor of 1, unchanged. GPS interference over the Gulf of Finland continues, and drones crossed during Ukraine's November raids on Baltic ports.
One above the floor of 1. Danish authorities say they foiled a Russian intelligence plot to kill a rapper before a concert, and expelled Russia's defence attaché. We do not log it yet.

developments.headline: Two Russian Kh-101 cruise missiles and a jet-powered drone crash in south-eastern Poland
developments.summary: Defence Minister Kosiniak-Kamysz said two Kh-101s fell at Nowy Lipowiec and Rudnik nad Sanem and a jet drone at Mołodycz. No one was hurt. One missile landed several hundred metres from buildings. Tusk said it looks like "an intentional provocation".
developments.russian_framing: We found no Kremlin or Defence Ministry comment on Poland. The Defence Ministry described the night as a strike on Ukraine's defence industry and energy targets (translated).

developments.headline: Poland asks allies for AWACS, F-35s and more Eastern Sentry assets; Trump calls the missiles a mistake
developments.summary: Poland requested allied AWACS aircraft, F-35s and more Eastern Sentry assets and personnel, but did not request Article 4 consultations. Trump told Fox News that Putin had been landing drones and "a couple of little missiles, by mistake" in Poland. Tusk replied: "God, protect us from such friends."

developments.headline: Denmark expels Russia's defence attaché over foiled plot to kill a Ukrainian-American rapper
developments.summary: Danish police said they foiled a September attempt by Russian intelligence to kill the rapper Kyivstoner before a concert. PET's chief said the plot was "planned by the Russian intelligence services". Løkke Rasmussen expelled the attaché and is weighing a halt to Schengen visas for Russians.
developments.russian_framing: Russia's embassy in Copenhagen says the accusations are "not backed by any evidence" (translated) and are meant to pressure the court.

developments.headline: Estonia decides to close all road crossings with Russia for six months from 1 December
developments.summary: The government will shut all five road crossings to people and vehicles from 1 December, for six months. PM Michal said Russia's hostile activities show "no signs of abating". The Foreign Ministry summoned Russia's chargé d'affaires.
developments.russian_framing: Russia's Foreign Ministry called the move "openly confrontational" (translated), summoned Estonia's chargé and reserved "political and diplomatic measures".

developments.headline: Moldova reports two drone incursions in one day
developments.summary: Ukrinform, citing Moldovan military statements, says a drone crossed north-east Moldova from 01:19 to 01:28 on 20 November. A second entered near Crocmaz in Ștefan Vodă at 14:48 and left within a minute. No damage was reported. We do not log either yet.

developments.headline: Russia launches more than 400 drones and 110 missiles at Ukraine and hits three Kyiv bridges
developments.summary: Zelensky said Russia launched more than 400 strike drones and over 110 missiles, 27 of them ballistic. The General Staff said 79 of 84 cruise missiles and 380 of 404 drones were downed or suppressed. Three Kyiv bridges were hit and at least nine people were killed.
developments.russian_framing: Russia's Defence Ministry said it struck Ukraine's defence industry, storage terminals, energy and transport targets with precision weapons (translated).

developments.headline: Polish prosecutors charge two Ukrainians with painting UPA slogans on monuments for Russian intelligence
developments.summary: The National Prosecutor's Office told PAP that Nikita S. and Dmytro Y. were detained in Poznań and charged. Prosecutors say Nikita S. acted "on behalf of Russian intelligence" for $500, painting "Sława UPA" on monuments to stir hatred between Poles and Ukrainians.
developments.russian_framing: Zakharova's 20 November briefing listed an item on "Polish-Ukrainian vandalism" (translated); we did not see its text.

developments.headline: Ukrainian drones hit the Dorogobuzh chemical plant in Smolensk Oblast
developments.summary: Drones struck the Dorogobuzh plant overnight into 20 November, Meduza reports, citing Astra and monitoring channels; eyewitness footage suggests a fire. The plant makes about 11% of Russia's ammonium nitrate and components for explosives. We found no Russian official confirmation.

categories.text: Estonian military intelligence says Russia lost about 149,000 troops in 12 weeks and recruitment is not keeping pace. Ukraine's General Staff reported 157 clashes on 20 November. Neither source reports a breakthrough.
Ukrainian drones hit the Dorogobuzh ammonium-nitrate plant in Smolensk Oblast (claimed only). Estonian intelligence estimates Russian refining capacity is down 30–55%.

One of the war's largest raids: more than 400 drones and 110 missiles, according to Zelensky. Three Kyiv bridges were hit and at least nine people killed. Routes over western Ukraine carried missiles into Poland.

Austria summoned Russia's ambassador over damage to its Kyiv embassy, and Estonia summoned Russia's chargé d'affaires. Moscow summoned Romania's ambassador over visas refused to a youth taekwondo team. We found no new movement in talks.

Two Kh-101s and a jet drone crashed in Poland's Lublin and Subcarpathian regions; air-raid alerts were issued in both. Moldova reported two drone entries on 20 November. We log none of these yet, pending host-government texts.

Denmark says it foiled a Russian intelligence plot to kill a rapper and expelled Russia's defence attaché. Polish prosecutors charged two Ukrainians with vandalising monuments on behalf of Russian intelligence.

We found no new ship hit off Bulgaria or Romania in the window. Bulgaria's PM Radev said Sofia cannot detect or destroy drones at sea and wants more NATO air patrols. Russia's Defence Ministry claimed strikes on vessels serving Ukraine.

Zakharova said NATO is "openly preparing for armed conflict with Russia" but that Russia has "no intention of attacking NATO member states" (translated). We found no new exercise or build-up near the Baltics or Finland.

Poland asked allies for AWACS, F-35s and more Eastern Sentry assets. Estonia will close its Russian land border from 1 December. The EU approved €1 billion from the European Peace Facility for Ukraine. Trump played down the Polish crashes as a "mistake".

strikes_new.summary: Ukrainian drones struck the Dorogobuzh plant overnight into 20 November, according to Astra and monitoring channels reported by Meduza and The Moscow Times. Eyewitness footage suggests a fire. The plant makes about 11% of Russia's ammonium nitrate and components for explosives. No Russian official confirmation found.

judgement.text:
We assess that 30-day spillover risk has risen within rung 4, mainly on the airspace and sabotage routes. The rung stays at 4. We log no new incident today. For Poland, Moldova and Denmark we could not open the host government's own statement, which is the standard we have applied all month. We expect to log the Polish case at rung 3, attribution 3, once we can. Airspace stays at four logged incidents in 30 days against a 90-day baseline of 14 a month, and the gap is mostly unlogged cases like today's.

The Polish crashes are the day's most important development. Notes from Poland and the Kyiv Independent report that Defence Minister Kosiniak-Kamysz identified two Kh-101s, at Nowy Lipowiec and Rudnik nad Sanem, and a jet drone at Mołodycz. One fell several hundred metres from buildings. Search results show this is the second Kh-101 to come down in Poland since 30 July. Tusk said "it does seem that we're dealing with an intentional provocation", and the defence minister linked the timing to nearby Coalition of the Willing drills. Poland did not shoot the objects down. It asked allies for AWACS, F-35s and more Eastern Sentry assets, not for Article 4 consultations. We assess a routing or guidance failure during a mass raid on western Ukraine as slightly likelier than a deliberate signal; see the competing explanations below. Either way, where the missile landed shows how a death on NATO soil could happen. We raise airspace from 15% to highly unlikely (20%) and F-2026-001 to 20%. A1 holds, because no Polish official has said Poland was the target.

Denmark's case widens the covert threat from property to people. CNN reports PET's chief saying the plot was "planned by the Russian intelligence services", and Copenhagen expelled Russia's defence attaché. Russia's embassy says the charges are "not backed by any evidence" (translated). Coming in the same week as Poland's foiled Kaliningrad plot, it leads us to raise sabotage from 30% to unlikely (35%). A4 holds.

Estonia's six-month border closure is defensive. Moscow called it "openly confrontational" (translated). Trump's "by mistake" remark, and Tusk's retort, show a gap between Washington and the frontline allies; that is the A2 risk to watch. On the ceasefire paradox, a 110-missile raid and Russia's rejection of truces keep near-term incident risk high and push medium-term reconstitution further out.
judgement.change_my_mind: If Polish investigators found the missiles flew a route aimed at Polish territory, or Russia owned the incursion, we would raise next-rung odds and review A1. A Russian admission of guidance failure, or a month of mass raids with no further incursions, would lower airspace odds.

competing_explanations.subject: Two Kh-101 missiles and a jet drone crash in south-eastern Poland, 20 November

hypotheses.label: Guidance or routing failure during a mass raid
hypotheses.assessment: Kh-101s routed over western Ukraine near the border in a raid of more than 110 missiles; strays fit spillover. No Polish official said Poland was the target.

hypotheses.label: Deliberate probe timed to Coalition of the Willing drills
hypotheses.assessment: Tusk and Kosiniak-Kamysz point to the timing near the drills at Nowa Dęba. This is a second Kh-101 since July, in a week when Poland says it foiled a Russian false-flag plot.

hypotheses.label: Ukrainian electronic warfare diverted the missiles
hypotheses.assessment: Jamming over western Ukraine could push missiles off course. No source we saw raises this.

forecasts_new.question: Will Polish authorities report a Russian missile or drone entering Polish airspace on a date between 21 November and 20 December 2026?
forecasts_new.resolution_criteria: Yes if Poland's Operational Command, defence ministry, prime minister or prosecutors state that a Russian missile or drone entered Polish airspace on a date between 21 November and 20 December 2026.
forecasts_new.base_rate_note: Russian missiles or drones entered Polish airspace on 30 July and 20 November 2026, about one case every two months, or roughly 35% over 30 days. Raised for winter mass raids routed over western Ukraine.

forecasts_new.question: Will Denmark announce a suspension of Schengen visa issuance to Russian nationals by 31 January 2027?
forecasts_new.resolution_criteria: Yes if the Danish government or foreign ministry announces, between 21 November 2026 and 31 January 2027, that Denmark suspends or stops issuing Schengen visas to Russian nationals, in general or for most categories.
forecasts_new.base_rate_note: Few EU states have unilaterally halted visas for Russians since the 2022 restrictions. Raised because Løkke Rasmussen said Denmark is weighing exactly this after the plot.

forecast_updates.note: Two Kh-101s crashed in Poland on 20 November; one landed several hundred metres from buildings. It is the second Kh-101 in Poland since July.
Poland asked allies for AWACS and F-35s after two Kh-101s crashed, but did not request Article 4. Tusk calls it a provocation.
Two more Moldovan drone entries on 20 November take our November count to about 11, pending a ministry tally.
Prosecutors confirmed charges against two Ukrainians acting for Russian intelligence, announced about 19 November. We are checking the detention dates before resolving.
The government formally decided on 20 November to close Narva-1, Narva-2, Koidula, Luhamaa and Saatse from 07:00 on 1 December.
Moldova reported two drone entries on 20 November, the first qualifying day in the window. Two more days are needed.

assumption_updates.reason: Tusk called the Kh-101 crashes a seemingly intentional provocation, but no official says Poland was targeted, and there was no damage or casualties. Not yet a deliberate, attributable armed attack.
Denmark's PET attributes a foiled assassination plot to Russian intelligence, and Poland charged two Russian-paid vandals. The covert campaign continues regardless of diplomacy.

taiwan: The most direct effect is on demand for air-defence and early-warning assets. Poland's request for allied AWACS, F-35s and more Eastern Sentry capacity adds to European competition for the same US-built systems and interceptors that Taiwan is waiting on, though one request will not shift delivery queues by itself. For Beijing, Trump's description of Kh-101s on allied soil as a "mistake" signals that Washington may tolerate grey-zone incursions on partners without a firm response; that is a precedent China can test with drones and balloons near Taiwan and Japan. The military lesson is in rules of engagement: Poland let two cruise missiles fly on rather than shoot them down in peacetime, the dilemma Taiwan faces with PLA drones near its outlying islands.

next_72h.event: Watch for Polish prosecutors' or Operational Command findings on the two Kh-101s and the jet drone, including their flight routes.
next_72h.why: A route aimed at Poland would challenge A1. Their statement would also let us log the incident.

next_72h.event: Watch for further Russian mass raids on western Ukraine and Odesa, and for drone entries into Moldova, Romania or Poland.
next_72h.why: Tests F-2026-031, F-2026-034 and the airspace odds after Putin's promise of 'more painful' retaliation.

next_72h.event: Watch for a Russian retaliatory expulsion of a Danish diplomat, and for Denmark's decision on Schengen visas for Russians.
next_72h.why: This would show whether the Danish case escalates diplomatically. It also tests F-2026-035.
